chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Ya'qub ibn Yazeed, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Qutham ibn Ka'b, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You are accustomed to performing Hajj.' I said: 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So let your final promise/covenant with the House be that you place your hand upon the Door and say: 'The beggar is at Your Door, so give in charity upon him with Paradise.'

key_terms.الْمِسْكِين: The beggar/poor one (referring to the supplicant's spiritual status)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and action when bidding farewell to the Kaaba during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses a companion known for frequenting the Kaaba, urging him to conclude his pilgrimage with a profound spiritual posture of humility. By placing his hand on the door and declaring himself a 'beggar' (al-miskin), the pilgrim seeks Paradise as a divine charity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *tawadu* (humility) and the concept of *sadaqah* extending beyond material wealth to the ultimate reward of Jannah.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Qusam Bin Ka’ab who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Are you habitual of the Hajj?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let the last of your Promises by the House (Kabah), that you place your hand upon the Door (of the Kabah), and you should be saying, ‘The beggar is at Your<sup>azwj</sup> Door, so Give in charity upon him with the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 5. Af-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ai-Nahdiy from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from ‘Abd Affah ibn Jabalah from Qutham ibn Ka‘b who has said the foilowing:

“Abu `Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, £ Do you perform al-Hajj very often?’ I replied, £ Yes, I do so.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘During your last farewell of the House, you should place your hand at the door and say, “The destitute is standing at Your door. Give him paradise as charity.’””
